newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Drug smuggling is being undertaken by London teenagers who are risking the death penalty in the Far East. The youngsters are being offered up to 20,000 stg by smuggling drugs from all over the world on behalf of heroin gangs. Customs officials believe there are currently up to 150 such British couriers.
- BOOTS GETS A TOEHOLD ON SHOPPING BY TV

At a time when many retailers are exploring time-saving alternatives to traditional shopping, Boots has launched an interactive TV shopping service in Hull, taking advantage of the council owned telephone service to allow customers to purchase toiletries via TV and telephone lines.
- JAPAN'S RESERVES SALE THREAT STOPS YEN SLIDE
The slump in the yen has been halted by the Japanese government threatening to sell foreign currency. On overnight markets the dollar dropped back by a tenth of a yen to 125.99.
- JUNK BOND MAKES A EUROPEAN DEBUT HIT

Swiss sanitaryware manufacturer Geberit made its market debut yesterday. The junk bond was issued by Merrill Lynch to the value of Dm157mn (56mn stg). Institutions have said it was oversubscribed by five times.
- POLITICIANS PUSHING FOR DEAL ON TOBACCO

Congress has been at the heart of current legislation bringing sweeping changes to the tobacco industry. Politicians have increased pressure on the industry to introduce new bills that would nearly treble the federal tax on cigarettes, force manufacturers to list ingredients, including carcinogens on each pack and penalise those whose advertising appeals to under-age smokers.
